name: Treaty with the Cherokee, October 27, 1805 (Tellico, South West Point cession)
promises: The Cherokee ceded the section of land on which the South West Point garrison stood, extending to Kingston, as a possible seat for the Tennessee assembly, reserving the ferries to themselves, and the first island in the Tennessee above the mouth of the Clinch (Article 1).
The Cherokee granted citizens free use of a mail road from Tellico to Tombigbee through their country (Article 2).
The United States would pay $1,600 in money or useful merchandise, at the Cherokee's option, within ninety days of ratification (Article 3).
compensation: $1,600 under Article 3. No Indian Claims Commission finding specific to this cession was found.
today: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians' claims under the Cherokee treaties of 1785 to 1835, Dockets 282-A through 282-L, were settled by compromise for $1,855,254.50 on September 11, 1972, after the parties compromised liability by stipulation; whether this treaty was among them was not established, and a compromise is not a finding of breach.

nationVoice.summary: The Nation's history says successive treaties with the British Crown and then the United States cut down the Cherokee Nation's original territory, and that further cessions confirmed in an 1819 treaty left most of the remaining Cherokee land in Georgia.

openQuestions: Royce cessions 58 and 59 in treaties.json were not checked against the schedule; the two parcels in Article 1 (the South West Point section and the island) fit two areas, but this was not confirmed.
Whether the Cherokee Nation (Oklahoma) brought its own Indian Claims Commission claim for the early eastern cessions was not established; only the Eastern Band's Docket 282 series was found.
Whether the $1,600 was paid, and whether the ferries reserved in Article 1 were respected, was not checked.
Cherokee Nation and Eastern Band accounts of this treaty were not located in this pass.
